clues.title: The programme in his pocket
clues.description: In Elias's breast pocket: the ceremony programme, annotated in his hand. Under the nine o'clock reading he has written his own title — 'The Bookkeeper's Apprentice, 1994' — and beneath it: 'Some debts the village forgot.'

clues.title: The missing year
clues.description: The archive boxes hold forty years of exercise books, labelled and shelved in Elias's exact order — 1992, 1993, then 1995. The 1994 volume is gone, and the gap in the row is fresh: the books either side have only just fallen together.

clues.title: The owl on the wrong side
clues.description: The cast-iron owl doorstop sits neatly beside the alley door — on the hinge side, where it never lives, and wiped clean while everything around it wears a week of dust. Something sticky has dried along the grip.

clues.title: Cinnamon on the iron
clues.description: The sticky trace on the owl's grip smells unmistakably of mulled cider — cinnamon, clove, orange peel. One stall at the fair served it, and whoever wiped this iron clean had spent the evening at the urn.

clues.title: The unbolted alley door
clues.description: The stockroom's alley door shows no forced entry — because none was needed. The inside bolt Priya swears she shot at six o'clock is drawn back. Whoever came this way was let in, or expected.

clues.title: The 1994 notebook, under the straw
clues.description: Deep in the cafe stall's crate of spare cups, under the straw: Elias's 1994 volume. Its last autumn entry, in a younger version of the same careful hand: 'M.B. at the schoolhouse window past nine again, tracing T.H.'s signature against the glass. Third evening running. Three days since we buried Thomas; one day before the bill of sale surfaced. I did not understand it then. I am afraid I do now.'

clues.title: The letter behind the frame
clues.description: In Marcus's study, the bill of sale for Hobbs Cafe hangs framed like a diploma — dated a month before Thomas Hobbs died. Folded behind the frame's backing board, a recent letter in Elias's hand: 'I re-read 1994. Sign the cafe to the village trust by Christmas, or the archive will read the page for you. You were my best pupil, Marcus. Arithmetic was never your weakness. — E.G.'

clues.title: "My notebooks remember"
clues.description: At 20:15 Elias announced from the bandstand that his notebooks would go to the village archive tonight, and that he would read one passage aloud himself at nine. 'My notebooks remember what the village finds convenient to forget.' Whoever needed those notebooks to stay shut had until nine o'clock.

clues.title: "Keep my name out of your books"
clues.description: At 20:10 Elias needled Owen about 'the church roof of 2015' loud enough for half the square. Owen went white, then red, and told him to keep Owen Price's name out of his damned books. Fifty minutes later, Elias was dead.

clues.title: The curation row
clues.description: At 19:50 Isabella confronted Elias at the ceremony table: nothing from the archive reaches the lectern unless she reads it first. Elias told her, smiling, that curation was a fine word for fear. She did not smile back.

clues.title: A thud under the band
clues.description: At 20:52, a single muffled thud sounded from the back rooms of the bookshop, almost lost under the band — inside the murder window, in the building where the body was found.

clues.title: "You know which page"
clues.description: At 20:25, standing next in the cider queue, Nadia heard Elias say quietly to Marcus over the urn: 'Come to the reading, Marcus. Or come and see me before it. You know which page.' Marcus went very still, and the ladle dripped.

clues.title: Grey coat in the dark alley
clues.description: From his van at about 20:44, Ben saw a man in a long grey overcoat, collar up, come out of the cafe's kitchen door and cross the dark alley to the bookshop's rear door — which opened to his hand. Ben never saw the face. But Marcus owns that coat, and the walk, Ben says, was 'that squared-off way of his, like the ground owes him rent.'

clues.title: Nineteen minutes for a box of cups
clues.description: Confronted with the grey coat, Clara stops covering: Marcus left the stall at 20:40 saying he'd fetch cups, and did not come back until 20:59 — empty-handed, out of breath, with a story about mice. The cafe's cup cupboard, she adds quietly, was full this morning.

clues.title: Owen's twenty dark minutes
clues.description: Owen says he left the brazier at about 20:40 'for logs' and was back by nine. Nobody saw him at his yard, the brazier never wanted for wood, and he bristles when pressed — leaving him, on his own account, unaccounted for across the murder window.

clues.title: The dressed burn
clues.description: Pressed, Nadia gives up what she promised to keep: Owen was with her in the clinic from 20:40 to nearly 21:00, having a second-degree burn dressed across his palm — his own brazier, two ciders and a rum. He swore her to silence because he'd sooner be a suspect than a punchline. The dressing is still on his hand.

clues.title: Isabella in the dark shop
clues.description: Clara, from the stall: at about 20:47 — inside the murder window — Isabella crossed the square, unlocked her own bookshop, and slipped inside without lighting the lamps. She came out six minutes later. The body was found in that building.

clues.title: Light under the stockroom door
clues.description: Isabella, cornered, gives up the rest of her six minutes: while she collected the ceremony glasses in the dark front room, there was lamplight under the stockroom door — and at ten to nine, a heavy thud from behind it. She told herself it was boxes settling and locked the shop on her way out. Someone was in that stockroom with Elias, and she stood twenty feet away.

clues.title: The tombola faces the shop
clues.description: Priya ran the tombola directly opposite the bookshop window, and watched Isabella the whole six minutes: counter lamp on, glasses down from the shelf, each one polished on her apron. She never went past the counter, and came out at 20:53 with a loaded tray — 'I remember, because the band had just finished The Weaving Song.'

clues.title: Ben's trip to the van
clues.description: Ben admits he left the stalls at about 20:43 and was at his van in the dark alley for a few minutes — 'checking the straps', he says, and checks his own shoes while he says it. The alley backs onto the room where Elias died.

clues.title: The lantern with the ring inside
clues.description: What Ben fetched from the van: a hand-built lantern painted with sweet peas — Priya's flower — with a ring taped inside the little door. He was going to propose at the nine o'clock lighting. Three weekends of secret work, smuggled to the tombola table under a delivery blanket, four minutes before the village changed the subject forever.

conclusions.summary: Marcus's ownership of Hobbs Cafe rests on a signature he forged thirty years ago — and Elias's 1994 notebook, due to be read at nine o'clock, recorded him practising it.
Marcus was inside the bookshop stockroom during the murder window — invited there by Elias, seen crossing the alley to its rear door, while his stall believed he was fetching cups.
The owl doorstop was wiped and replaced by hands sticky with the cafe stall's mulled cider — and the notebook taken from the dead man's boxes surfaced under Marcus's own stall.
Elias was struck once from behind with the stockroom's cast-iron owl doorstop at 20:52 — the thud heard through the stockroom door.
Marcus's claim that he barely left the stall is false: he was gone nineteen minutes, came back with no cups, and the errand he invented never happened.
Owen publicly threatened Elias over what the notebooks say about the church roof of 2015, fifty minutes before the murder.
Owen vanished from the brazier for the entire murder window with a firewood story nobody can confirm.
Owen spent the murder window in the clinic having a burn dressed — a fact he hid out of wounded pride, not guilt.
Isabella fought Elias over control of the archive, then entered the murder building, in the dark, inside the murder window.
Priya watched Isabella through the lit shop window for the whole six minutes — she never went past the counter, and left carrying a loaded tray.
Ben was at his van in the dark alley — twenty feet from the murder room — during the window, and squirms when asked why.
Ben was fetching the proposal lantern he'd hidden in the van — a secret kept from Priya, not from the police.
